title: Reaction Offers
description: What a player sees when the game offers a reaction: what happened, who did it, and what they can do now, shaped like the engine's real decision (context.trigger from the new DecisionTrigger).

shots.heading: Sabotage after an action card was played
shots.caption: What happened names the player (faction and colour), the card (Uprising) and its full printed text, with a Shrink link. You can now says "Before this resolves, you can play Sabotage", with the card's printed window and text. Play Sabotage, Pass, Compact card text and Pin sit below.

shots.heading: A system with your units was activated
shots.caption: The activated system is named with its planets, links to the map (Show on map) and notes how many of the viewer's units stand there; Decoy Operation is offered with its window ("After another player activates a system that contains 1 or more of your structures").

shots.heading: Ships moved into a system
shots.caption: The engine's SHIP_MOVED now carries the destination and the arriving ships: "moved ships into System 26: 2 cruisers, 1 dreadnought", then Rescue.

shots.heading: Two different cards for one window
shots.caption: The inner step repeats the same trigger and lists each card with its window and full text, with one Play button per card.

shots.heading: Phone width (390 px)
shots.caption: One scrolling column: what happened, you can now, then Play / Pass.

shots.heading: No trigger data (older server)
shots.caption: Without a trigger the dialog says only which window opened, in words ("A reaction window opened: after a ship is destroyed"), never an engine identifier.

shots.heading: A card shrunk to its first sentence
shots.caption: A player who knows Plague shrinks it: only the first sentence stays, with Show full text. The choice is remembered per card; Compact card text shrinks every card. New players see everything in full.

notes.title: Fixed since the first capture
notes.text: The three earlier gaps are fixed: the dialog names what was reacted to and who did it, the button reads "Play Sabotage" (built from the card name), and no engine identifier appears inside the dialog.

notes.title: Mock artifact: the orange banner
notes.text: The banner above the board prints the pending subtype because this mock reuses it as the turn status stage. A real server sends "Waiting for player" there.

notes.title: Remaining
notes.text: The per-card "never offer again" switch is not in the dialog yet (phase 3: it needs a server message and engine wiring), and the public waiting notice for other seats does not name the trigger yet (phase 4).
